title: What the Webb Telescope Sees

endcard.line: Pictures: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI; NASA/MSFC (public domain)

segments.say: These towers of gas and dust are where new stars are born. The James Webb Space Telescope can see right through them.

anim.title: The Webb telescope
items: Built by NASA, ESA and Canada

segments.say: Webb was launched on Christmas Day, twenty twenty-one. It is the largest telescope ever sent into space.
Its mirror is six and a half metres wide: eighteen hexagons, coated with a thin layer of gold.

left.title: Visible light
items: Light from the first galaxies is stretched

segments.say: Webb sees infrared, heat light. Infrared passes through dust, and catches light from the earliest galaxies, stretched on its long journey.
To see heat, it must stay very cold. It sits one and a half million kilometres away, behind a sunshield the size of a tennis court.
It looks for the first galaxies, for stars being born, and even for the gases in the air of planets around other stars.
For Prelims: Webb is an infrared telescope at the second Lagrange point, and the successor to Hubble.

quiz.q: Which kind of light does Webb mainly see?
quiz.why: Infrared passes through dust and catches stretched early light.
About 1.5 million km away at L2.
